subject: radiography
intro: Radiography leads to the imaging professions — the technologists who operate the X-ray, CT, MRI and nuclear medicine equipment that lets clinicians see inside the body.

roles.title: Radiologic Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Take X-rays and CT scans and administer nonradioactive materials into a patient's bloodstream for diagnosis — positioning patients, controlling image quality, and specialising in other scanning modalities.
roles.where: Unit 1's X-ray production and exposure factors, unit 3's digital detectors, positioning and artefacts, and units 4 and 5's chest, spine, trauma and CT procedures are the core syllabus of the job; unit 6's dose limits govern every exposure.

roles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Technologists
roles.what: Operate MRI scanners — monitoring patient safety and comfort, checking the quality of images during the scan, administering gadolinium contrast intravenously, and entering patient history and scan parameters into the computer.
roles.where: Unit 5's MRI principles and unit 3's image production and quality control are the technical heart; unit 2's contrast agents and venipuncture map to gadolinium administration; unit 6's protection mindset carries into MRI safety zones.

roles.title: Nuclear Medicine Technologists
roles.what: Prepare, administer and measure radioactive isotopes in therapeutic, diagnostic and tracer studies — calculating doses, operating radioisotope equipment and running studies that track how the body functions.
roles.where: Unit 1's radiation physics and unit 6's radiation biology and protection are the safety backbone; unit 5's cross-sectional imaging links to the SPECT and PET side of the work; unit 3's quality control covers the instrument checks.

roles.title: Radiation Therapists
roles.what: Operate the equipment that delivers prescribed doses of radiation to cancer patients — following the treatment plan precisely across a course of sessions, positioning patients and monitoring them through therapy.
roles.where: Unit 6 — dose limits, justification and optimisation, protection of staff and public — is the daily discipline; unit 1's X-ray production and unit 5's imaging principles underpin treatment localisation and verification.
